senses.gloss:
daityas
(‘sons of दिति’)
------------------------------------------
The Hindu mythological lore is replete with the stories of constant wars and conflicts between the सुरस् and the असुरस्, the देवस् and the दानवस्.
The sage कश्यप has been projected by these stories as the progenitor of all living beings. He had thirteen wives, all of whom were daughters of दक्ष-प्रजापति. Among these, अदिति, दिति and Danu were more well-known.
The sons of अदिति are ādityas or āditeyas (same as देवस् or सुरस् or gods), of दिति, the दैत्यस् and of Danu, the दानवस्. Sometimes the असुरस्, the दैत्यस् and the दानवस् (as also the राक्षसस्) are bracketed together. They seem to be the archetypes of violent, greedy and sinful beings. However, even from among them great persons like प्रह्लाद, बलि and बाण had been born and their lives as men of virtue and devotees of God had been exemplary.
